title: Move inside a branch view destroys the file
detail: virtualItem returns the real file for vfolder://.../d/a.txt so FileJob plans .write(replacing: true). In put the two providers differ, so the file is stream-copied to a temp, renamed over itself, then removed at 539-541. targetsSourceFolder is false for a move and the paste filter compares a file: folder with a vfolder: one. Steps: open a branch view, Cmd+X then Cmd+V on a file in the branch root, or F6/Shift+F6 and type the same name in another letter case. Observed: job reports completed=1, no error, no question; a.txt and c.txt gone from disk. Scope: only files directly in the branch root; a file from a subfolder is moved up into the root, and a copy is refused with 'cannot copy a file to itself'.

title: FIFO hangs a streamed transfer
detail: LocalFileSystem.read opens with a blocking FileHandle(forReadingFrom:); no cancellable variant, default only checks the flag before opening. isSpecial is not consulted in FileJob. Steps: copy a folder containing a named pipe to an archive, server or other file system. Observed: not finished after 3 s, not finished 3 s after cancel(), ended only when the pipe's write end was opened. Quit: applicationShouldTerminate returns .terminateLater and waits for the job with no timeout (read, app not launched). Scope: plain local-to-local copy does not hang (uses copy; pipe not copied); local-to-local with follow links on a link to a pipe does hang.

title: Several sources onto one target name overwrite each other
detail: Job only waits for the first file to land; plan then treats it as an ordinary existing target. Observed (Move, Overwrite all): s/a/x.txt and s/b/x.txt into t/ gave completed=2, one x.txt containing 'from-b', both sources gone, no question. Report.txt and report.txt from a case-sensitive source onto APFS left one file with 'lower'. Same with and without the parallel pool. Narrower than worded: in default Ask mode the Overwrite question does appear for the second file; real loss needs Move plus Overwrite all (preset or answered earlier); with Copy the sources survive.

title: Resume onto a symlink destination rewrites the link's target
detail: A link has size 0 so guard at 617 passes and the dialog offers Resume. resumeInPlace compares zero bytes, then LocalFileSystem.append opens with O_WRONLY, follows the link and truncates. Steps: copy f.txt to a folder where f.txt is a link, choose More > Resume. Observed: elsewhere/victim.txt (53 bytes) now contains 'source-bytes'; link still a link.

title: 2-second timestamp tolerance applied on every volume
detail: Unconditional. On APFS with 'Overwrite all older', a source 1.5 s newer was skipped and one 2.5 s newer was copied. Also affects 'older or same' and 'rename older, skip newer'.

title: Delete and Move descend through mount points
detail: deleteTree/deleteChildren and transferFolder have no device check (BranchWalker and DirectoryTree do). Delete: a permanent delete (not Trash) of a folder containing a mounted disk image erased everything on that volume; only error was 'Resource busy' for the mount point itself. Move: merging into an existing folder (item by item) emptied the mounted volume into the destination; content survives but the disk is emptied. Reproduced with real mounts.

title: Link-cycle detection is textual
detail: resolvingLink uses URL.isInside/isSameLocation which are string prefix tests. Steps: copy with follow links a folder containing loop -> . reached through a symlinked parent path. Observed: direct path gave 1 copy; through the alias gave 31 nested copies, 32 levels deep, stopped only by the kernel's link limit. Not tested: with k such links per folder growth would be about k^31; counting pass measure has the same test.

title: Keep partial files breaks Retry
detail: Option renames the partial to the real name; Retry re-runs the same .write(replacing: false) plan and 724 fails with 'already exists'. Observed: error 1 injected failure, error 2 '.../big.bin already exists'; 4-byte partial stayed, job did not complete. With option off Retry succeeded. No data loss.

title: '755' over 4755 keeps setuid (deliberate)
detail: Comment at 19-20 documents it. Observed: '755' gives 4755, 'rwxr-xr-x' gives 4755, '0755' gives 755. Differs from chmod 755; dialog hint does not mention it.

title: lockedCopies allows silent unlock-and-delete (narrower form)
detail: Not affected: user's own locked original is refused; a locked file copied by a job is refused afterwards because the entry is dropped on the temp-to-final rename (461). Affected: a locked folder copied by a job stays in the table (via copyMetadata, 617); deleting that copy later in the same session removed it with no 'locked' question while a control folder did get the question. A direct copy() to a final name behaves the same even after user unlocks and re-locks by hand; no in-app caller does that today. Wipe at 4,096 (478): read only, not reproduced; consequence would be a spurious 'Operation not permitted' on a pending locked temp, not a deletion.
basis: CONFIRMED (ran) in narrower form; 4,096-entry wipe read only

title: setAttributes on a symlink changes its target
detail: Observed: target went 644 to 600 and took the new date; link unchanged. Change Attributes guards against this (AttributeChange.swift:333). Unguarded callers: FileJob:745 and 1367 (see N1) and SyncPlan.swift:192, 389, 392 (read, not run).

title: write() creates the file 0644 until close
detail: Permissions applied only at close. Observed: mode 644 while open, 600 after close. Scope: streamed transfers only (from archives or servers, followed links, Append, non-in-place Resume); local copies use copyfile and are not affected. Matters only in folders other users can enter.

title: append/read block on FIFOs
detail: Non-regular-file check at 376 comes after the blocking open. Observed: both still blocked after 2 s. At job level, Resume onto a destination pipe hung in startsWithPartial and ignored Cancel.

title: Format.kilobytes traps near Int64.max
detail: Int64.max crashes with signal 5 in debug and release; Int64.max - 512 is fine. Reach unproven: callers pass saturating sums so value reachable in principle (e.g. server listing with absurd sizes); whether remote parsers clamp sizes was not checked.

title: totalSizeByListing recursion is unbounded
detail: With a fake provider on a 512 KB thread stack a release build survives 2,000 levels and crashes at 4,000; debug crashes between 300 and 400. Local disks cannot nest that deep (path limit; LocalFileSystem has its own totalSize). Needs crafted archive or hostile server; not built. Related: FileJob's measure, deleteTree and transferFolder recurse per level too; not tested.

title: Network move(replacing: true) loses both files (as worded)
detail: Claim as worded REFUTED: moving ftp:/ro/a.txt (folder not writable) to ftp:/w/ with Overwrite sent RNFR, RNTO 550, DELE /w/a.txt, RNFR, RNTO 550; target gone, source intact, move failed.

title: Network move deletes destination after any refused rename (underlying defect)
detail: Code deletes the destination after any refused rename whatever the reason. move(missing.txt -> keep.txt, replacing: true) deleted keep.txt even though the source never existed. Plain-rename SFTP path feeds the same branch (read, not run). By reading only: for an upload with Overwrite, discard (FileJob:731) then removes the temp, leaving nothing on the server though local source remains; for Append (FileJob:862-866) the existing remote file would be lost outright.

title: Deleting a symlink the system refuses with EPERM chmods the link's target
detail: removing answers the 'locked' question by calling setAttributes(item.permissions | 0o200) on the URL, which for a link lands on its target (claim 11). Steps: delete a link inside a locked folder (sticky folder with foreign-owned link should behave the same), answer the locked question yes. Observed: delete still failed and the link's target private/key.pem went from 600 to 755. Permissions exposure, not data loss. discard (745) has the same pattern for a locked temp.

title: Deadlock at quit between archive flush and credential prompt
detail: flush() holds flushLock for its whole duration incl. upload(); upload() calls provider.write on the server file system; a (re)connect can ask a question via askCredentials/askToTrust/askSecret, which go through DispatchQueue.main.sync; main in applicationWillTerminate calls archive.flush() and waits on flushLock. Sequence: ZIP on FTP/SFTP with pending changes; flush timer thread in upload() needs a new connection; user quits, main blocks on flushLock; connection asks a question, timer thread blocks in main.sync. Narrow: question must be posted after main entered applicationWillTerminate (else a modal dialog is already up). NetworkPlugin.stop runs before ArchivesPlugin.stop and empties sessions, so a write after that builds a fresh session which asks if password not in Keychain. User sees beachball at quit, force quit needed, edit never reaches server.

title: Coalescer.settle calls onChange off the main thread
detail: 510/517 schedule settle() on DispatchQueue.global; 516 calls fire() there with no hop to main. Callback is reloadChangedPanels, which mutates missedChanges and calls panel.reload (MainThread.assert at PanelViewController:810); contract says main thread. Sequence: panel shows a branch view or search-result list; second change report within 0.5 s of first; FSEvents latency is also 0.5 s so under sustained changes it often lands just before settle. User sees assertion crash in debug; in release undefined behaviour, possible crash.

title: Archive eviction race: slot dropped while a writer is starting
detail: Race CONFIRMED: store.archive(at:) releases the slot lock on return; caller then takes the archive's own lock and sets openWriters += 1; in between evict can see isBusy == false and drop the slot (comment at 155-157 is wrong). Window a few instructions, needs at least 12 other archives open plus another thread opening one right then. Stated consequence REFUTED for file jobs: FileJob.put writes under a temp name then renames; rename resolves the archive again, gets a fresh OpenArchive from disk and fails 'not found' (OpenArchive:876); source kept. What does happen: spurious error on one file (Retry works) and the orphan's own timer later writes a stray .afm-<uuid>.tmp member into the ZIP. Weaker variant holds: DirectorySync writes directly under final name (SyncPlan:272, write at 358); commit succeeds as a no-op; data exists only in the orphan until its timer fires; if app quits first flushAll (line 184) skips orphans and store.close() deletes the spool; sync does not delete the source. Further double race: orphan and fresh archive check the file signature under different locks (OpenArchive:1272-1274) so one flush could overwrite the other.
basis: PARTLY CONFIRMED: race CONFIRMED (read); stated consequence REFUTED for file jobs; weaker variant in DirectorySync holds

title: FileSearch.Walk data race on cancel
detail: On cancel deliver leaves its wait with pending > 0 and writes node.candidates = [] under the lock; a worker that just left the lock at 423 reads node.candidates unlocked (two reads of .count at 433, array copy at 440). Only with a text pattern or field rules (needed true); without cancellation the wait at 367 prevents it; after cancel deliver sweeps sibling nodes at 375, widening the set. User sees possible crash cancelling a content search: use-after-free on the array buffer, or trap at 433 if count goes N to 0 between two reads (range lower bound above upper).

title: FTPReader.close() cuts a connection already returned to the pool
detail: close() snapshots active under stateLock and calls running?.connection.interrupt() after unlocking; interrupt() at 693-698 does it under the lock with an explaining comment. Sequence: reader hits EOF between 706 and 710, releases connection to the pool, another thread takes it, then close() closes its sockets. Closing thread must be preempted for a server round trip between two adjacent statements. User sees 'connection lost' on an unrelated transfer or rename/delete; repeatable commands reconnect silently (perform, 320).
basis: CONFIRMED (read) as a race, very narrow window

title: LocalFileSystem.places() blocks 1 s per call on main
detail: Computes a new 1 s deadline on every call and waits while knownPlaces == nil, which stays nil until first readPlaces() returns (calls mountedVolumeURLs with resource values). Main-thread callers listed. User sees with a dead network mount at launch 1 s freezes at start-up, on every volume-menu open and on every mount notification. mountedVolumeURLs hang not induced.

title: OpenArchive.capabilities takes a lock on main
detail: Reached on main from command validation. Correction: lock not held across member data or archive rewrite (build, 1062, runs outside it); held across metadata system calls on the archive's volume: access() at 686, statfs/free-space at 850, clonefile probe at 772, stat/open/rename in install 1268-1274, stat at 482, full re-read of ZIP directory in rebase 1313-1327. Nothing visible on a local SSD; stall on a slow or stalled network share.

title: realpath on main for every location change
detail: Worse than stated: every location change passes both panels' directories; if one panel sits on a dead mount each navigation in the healthy panel runs realpath on the dead path on main. UI freeze on each navigation until the mount times out.

title: ViewerPane.stopWork closes remote readers on main
detail: SFTP closeHandle is a synchronous request with 30 s default timeout; FTP stop() -> abortTransfer() waits up to 10 s for a reply. Up to one idle reader per core closed one after another. Freeze when closing the viewer or switching quick-view file while server is slow.

title: Blocked global-queue threads from PanelLoader.stream starve GCD pool
detail: Workers on DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated); Listing.swift calls provider.parent, root and volume(of:), plain system calls with no cancellation. Measured (16 cores, macOS 27.0.1): 200 blocks in a blocking read(): only 80 ever started; then probes on global at every QoS did not run within 3 s, asyncAfter on global did not run, a private serial queue still ran. A local folder load goes to the same global queue and starves, as do file jobs and archive flush timers. Caveats: quiet reloads do not stack (816-820), only explicit refreshes and navigations add a thread; not tested with a real dead mount.
basis: CONFIRMED (read + ran) mechanism; needs about 80 stuck threads

title: Parallel workers always take the oldest job
detail: open.first; threads added by watchLater take the same job. Measured: 64 CPU pieces of 50 ms took 0.24 s on 16 threads alone, 3.73 s on 1 thread beside an older job whose pieces sleep; sleeping job grew to 61 threads. Later job not blocked (caller always works on it) but loses all parallelism until the older job has handed out every piece.

title: No autorelease pool on Parallel pool threads
detail: Bodies run with no pool; no autoreleasepool anywhere in Sources. Measured (same read as LocalFileSystem:343, 2048 MiB in waves through the real pool): malloc in use at end 1908 MiB as in the project vs 0 MiB with autoreleasepool around each piece. In-use dropped to 0 once threads exited after 2 s idle but process footprint stayed at 1920 MiB. One pass over a 4 GiB file holds about 4 GiB. 'Tens of GB' figure unproven (needs repeated passes without a 2 s pause; not measured in app).
basis: CONFIRMED (ran) mechanism; 'tens of GB' figure unproven

title: A stuck job blocks commands and Quit
detail: applicationShouldTerminate returns .terminateLater; reply sent only when the queue empties, which happens only after work returns; isBusy rejects every command not marked runsDuringJobs. User sees beeps on most commands, queued jobs never start, Quit does nothing; force quit. A job counts as stuck if work never returns after cancel, or never starts because the global pool is exhausted (claims 10 and 14).

title: One GCD thread parked per launched program
detail: Both branches sit in ended.wait() until the login shell exits. Lines turned into open -a return at once; a program run directly holds a thread for its lifetime. These threads count toward the 80-thread limit measured under claim 10.

title: Every local read loop has the autorelease-retention problem (claim 12 class)
detail: In isolation a GCD block reading 200 MiB through FileHandle.read(upToCount:) held 200 MiB until the block ended. Same reader used with no pool in: FileJob:813 (stream copy local to server or archive; whole job is one block), Checksum.swift:21, DuplicateFinder.swift:121, TextPattern.swift:314-347 (on search threads that live for the whole search, FileSearch.swift:461), SyncComparison.swift:342, ToolRun.swift:135. Memory would grow by roughly the bytes read. Not measured in the app.
basis: measured (isolated block); not measured in app

title: Pool exhaustion chains into the Quit hang
detail: Once 80 global-queue threads are blocked, a new job's work never starts, isBusy stays true and Quit hangs.

title: The Parallel pool grows through a global queue so it stops adding threads when the global pool is exhausted
detail: Pool growth goes through a global queue, so it stops adding threads in the same state (80 blocked global threads).

title: Orphaned archives are skipped at quit and their spool files deleted
detail: flushAll iterates only the table, then store.close() deletes the spool files of orphaned archives, so pending edits there are lost.

title: File names run as shell code through ShellWords.escaped (grapheme bug)
detail: Real ParameterExpansion.swift compiled with a stub FileItem.split, expanded lines passed to /bin/zsh -c and /bin/bash -c; marker files created by touch text from the file name. ShellWords.escaped compares whole Swift Characters so ", `, \ or $ followed by a combining mark is not escaped; needsQuoting works on scalars so value is still wrapped in "..." which the name closes. Line 284 single-quote path has the same flaw (replacingOccurrences of ' does not match ' + U+0301). Line goes unchanged to $SHELL -l -c. Name a"́;touch M1;"́ created on APFS and listed back byte for byte. Affected with any template even plain 'cmd %N': %N %n %v %V %M %m %O %o %E %e %P %p %T %t %S %s %R %r %B %C1-9; same codes inside user's own "..." or '...'; in-quote %S path (428); %|VAR| and %VAR% in Command field (not attacker-controlled in practice); %P/%T when a folder name carries the payload. Not affected: %L %F %D %UL %UF %WL %WF (list file), cd or internal cm_ steps; %Q switches quoting off by design. Precondition: crafted file/folder name in a visited folder (extracted archive, download, share, FTP listing) and user running any user command, button or Start-menu entry with one of those codes with cursor/selection on it. Arbitrary code as the user.

title: File names run as shell code through quote-state tracking with particular templates (ASCII names)
detail: Plain ASCII names execute with particular templates: "$(cmd %N)" with name 'g x;touch M7' or 'e";touch M5;"' (value escaped for double quotes but in a fresh $(...) context); `cmd %N` with 'f$(touch M6)' (backticks strip the \ from \$); $'%N' with 'h\';touch M8;'' (backslash live inside $'...'); '%N # don't' + newline + '%N' with 'g x;touch M7' (apostrophe in a comment flips quote state; needs multi-line field). Here-docs are the same class but not run.

title: $SHELL -l -c fails silently under csh/tcsh
detail: /bin/tcsh -l -c 'echo hi' and /bin/csh both print 'Unknown option: -l' and exit 1. In CommandRunner.launch output goes to the null device and exit status is never read, so the command silently does nothing. SystemToolsPlugin.swift:143 has the same flags. Functional bug, not security.

title: Panel drop accepts afm.panel-item from any pasteboard with no drag-source check
detail: No draggingSource check in validateDrop/acceptDrop. Precondition: user drags from a hostile app onto a panel. Any URL scheme gets in (ftp://, archive://, vfolder://), so a drop can start a connection or transfer; confirmation shows only if confirmsDrops is on.

title: Download-list run overwrites files with no preview
detail: No preview after the file-name prompt; move(arrived, to: to, replacing: true) reaches plain rename(2). List also accepts put:, copy:, move:, so it can upload or move local files. Precondition: user runs a list file someone else wrote. ftp://evil/x -> ~/.zshenv silently replaces an existing file; copy step only asks if the source's own name exists.

title: Download-list line injection via server-supplied names
detail: isSafeName rejects only / and NUL; DownloadList.parse splits on every Unicode newline. No / allowed per name so payload needs nested remote folder names. Precondition: malicious server, then 'Add to download list', then run.

title: HTML meta refresh navigation loads remote content in page mode
detail: RichViews allows every .other navigation; CSP does not cover navigation. Headless WKWebView with same config fetched http://127.0.0.1:18473/refresh and showed it. JavaScript stayed off; ,

title: RTF/PDF hostile links in the viewer
detail: RTF: NSAttributedString(rtf:) kept x-evil-scheme://... and file:///...Calculator.app as .link and the viewer has no clickedOnLink or PDFViewDelegate; parsing CONFIRMED, what AppKit opens on click not shown. PDF: unproven. Precondition: user clicks a link.
basis: PARTLY CONFIRMED (RTF parse only; opening unproven; PDF unproven)

title: Remote URL last path component traversal overwrites a local file (viewer download primitive)
detail: lastPathComponent of ftp://h/a/..%2F..%2Fx returns ../../x on this OS, giving <folder>/../../x; createFile truncates an existing file. Listings cannot produce this (appending(name:) encodes %). Routes: followLink loads any absolute href from a viewed page, tab files, typed URLs, cm_List <url>. Only .media/.other content takes this path. Precondition: malicious server plus viewed page and a click, or crafted URL. Medium if chain works: server-chosen path overwritten with server content.
basis: PARTLY CONFIRMED: primitive CONFIRMED (ran), full chain unproven

title: Configuration import writes every key and has no confirmation
detail: restore writes every key in the file, not only known ones; validate checks shape only; no summary or confirmation. Password lookup by UUID alone. Precondition: user imports hostile file; password redirect also needs victim's connection UUID (in their own export). High for the import: user commands plus key bindings mean code runs on next keypress, and network.trustedCertificates can be pre-seeded. Low-medium for the redirect.

title: Downloaded files carry no quarantine attribute
detail: No quarantine code in Sources/Plugins/Network; protocol default returns nil; Info.plist has no quarantine key. Malicious or compromised server, user opens download: no Gatekeeper prompt. Low-medium.

title: Only ZIP encryption is the weak legacy cipher and the dialog does not warn
detail: Sole cipher; its comment calls it weak; dialog says only 'Encrypt (ZIP only)'. Precondition: someone obtains the archive. Medium for anyone relying on it.

title: Credential leak through VirtualLocation.prefix(of:) user-info
detail: prefix(of:) would copy user-info, but panel URLs are built without credentials. Only a hand-written ftp://u:p@host/ in a tab file or afm.panel-item could carry one. Negligible.

title: Password in typed address appears in mount-error alert
detail: VolumeMounting puts url.absoluteString in the alert; NetworkCommands echoes typed text. Precondition: user typed smb://user:pass@host and the mount failed. On-screen only; no log write found but ui.report not traced to the end.

title: Password saved despite unticking 'save password'
detail: edit() deletes it when unticked; the caller then sees none stored and saves profile.password. Precondition: quick connect with password in the address, then 'save session' on disconnect.

title: FTPS: changed certificate gets the same trust dialog as a new one
detail: A new fingerprint for a host that already has an accepted one gets the same dialog; 'Always trust' appends. On-path attacker against a server with a self-signed certificate. Medium for FTPS.

title: SFTP: changed host key handled by dialog
detail: SFTP uses /usr/bin/ssh with no StrictHostKeyChecking override, so the system ssh handles a changed key rather than this dialog.

title: Active-mode FTP data listener accepts first connection with no peer check
detail: NWListener(using: .tcp, on: .any), first connection wins, no peer check. Passive mode correctly reuses the control peer. Precondition: active mode (not default), plain FTP, attacker reaching the port in the window. Low.

title: Archive path split on Character lets ../ + combining mark land one level up
detail: Splits on Character. '../́escaped.txt' and '../‍e3.txt' (U+0301, U+200D) landed in the parent of the destination. Exactly one level up, name must begin with the combining character so no known file can be targeted. Precondition: user unpacks hostile archive. Ran the two copied lines, not the full Unpacker.

title: Foreign-format archive named as mtree text pulls local files into the listing (bsdtar)
detail: An mtree text file named evil.7z with contents=<marker> produced a tar holding the marker's content. Any file not ZIP, TAR, gz, bz2 or xz takes this path. Local files copied into the listing or extraction; no exfiltration by itself.

title: Archive files created with 0644 regardless of source modes
detail: Member modes inside are preserved. Another local user can read.

title: Tab file entry count
detail: File capped at 1 MiB, still roughly 100k tabs; count claim bounded.

title: Tab file text() writes paths and captions unescaped; loaded active tab connects at once
detail: A loaded active tab is shown at once; ftp://user:pw@host is announced without asking. Precondition: hostile .tab file, or a folder name with a newline that the user saves and reloads. Low.

title: Configuration export is world-readable and includes sensitive data
detail: Export takes every JSON-valued key in the defaults domain: command history, connection hosts, users and UUIDs, trusted fingerprints, tabs. Data.write(.atomic) gave mode 644 under umask 022. Tree cache is plain text in Application Support. Another local user or wherever export is shared; cache informational.

title: Catastrophic regex backtracking in FTP LIST parsing
detail: Worse than claimed. One line of '-rwxrwxrwx ' plus N digits took 3.4 s at 5,000, 20 s at 10,000, 78 s at 20,000, 268 s at 40,000. No line cap; readLine and the reply buffer are unbounded. Malicious FTP server; user opens any folder: one ~40 KB line holds a thread for minutes, many lines hold every core, a server that never sends a newline exhausts memory.

title: followLink loads any absolute URL in the viewer
detail: Any href that is not http, https or mailto is opened in the viewer, including file:///... and other servers. This is the route that makes claim 5 reachable.

title: Unbounded FTP listing remainder re-split on every block (quadratic time, unbounded memory)
detail: rest is re-split in full on every 256 KB block, so a long line without a newline costs quadratic time and unbounded memory, separately from the regex.

title: Link-first extraction (symlink then file through the link) unproven
detail: Unpacker creates symlinks with any target. Within one run folders are created first so a 'link, then file through the link' archive should fail; a second archive unpacked into the same folder would follow an existing link. Not tested.

title: Verifier run side effects
detail: Regex timing test for claim 16 used about six minutes of CPU; a ksh -l / dash -l probe sourced the user's ~/.profile (read only, printed a syntax error); marker files left in c13/ and c16/root/ under the scratch folder. App never launched; tests ran on copies of the code.

title: Segment.thin traps on overflow
detail: When a segment has more checkpoints than bytes, bytes/count is 0 so 0*step < 4096 holds forever and step *= 2 overflows after 62 doublings (crash report 'arithmetic overflow' at line 225). Trigger: one line starting in a 4 MiB segment producing more than 4,194,304 checkpoints (>~268 million rows): a 300 MB line at width 1, or a 10 GB line under about 37 columns. Width 1 settable (allows 1..16384); with window width the floor is 20 columns. Direct call with 5 checkpoints over 4 bytes traps; TextRowIndex.build with 64-byte segments and a 12,288-byte line at width 1 traps; controls just under the limit return. Consequence: app crashes at end of indexing. 'Never terminates' part REFUTED.
basis: CONFIRMED (ran) as a trap; 'never terminates' REFUTED

title: CharacterBoundaries indexes past data on a shrunk file
detail: Both index data up to the requested length not the length returned. Trigger: text in code page 932/936/949/950, file truncated after loading, then a search reaching a chunk past the first. With a source reporting 200,000 bytes but returning 50,000, characterStart traps at 106 and ViewerSearch.find traps at 78; control with full file returns 150000. Crash; other encodings never reach this code.

title: Save As onto the viewed file can empty it
detail: createFile(atPath:contents:nil) replaces the file with an empty one before any read but with a new inode. Normal case: ProviderByteSource usually holds an idle reader on the old inode; a 5,000,000-byte file saved onto itself intact. Failing case: after source.close() the same save left 0 bytes and no error because guard !block.isEmpty else { break } (557) returns success. Unproven: natural trigger where all idle readers are checked out by a running parallel index build so the save opens a fresh reader on the empty file (reading only).

title: Viewer measuring loop cannot be cancelled
detail: No flag check inside the loop; relies on reader.interrupt() which the local reader does not implement (default does nothing). LocalFileSystem.item(at:) uses lstat and reports size 0 for anything not a regular file; a symlink to a 5,000-byte file has size 0. Run: opening a symlink to /dev/zero and cancelling at 0.3 s was still reading at 5.3 s; no control with a regular file or larger timeout, so it shows the loop outliving cancel, not how long. Consequence from the code: a symlink to a large file is read to the end before anything shows, endless device never finishes.
basis: CONFIRMED (read); reproduced in one run only

title: flushAll single pass loses edits in nested archives at quit
detail: Iterates a dictionary once. Flushing the inner archive uploads into the outer one making the outer pending again. ArchivesPlugin.stop() calls it once then store.close(). Run: with a 600 KB inner archive the change was lost in 5 of 10 runs; with a tiny inner archive 0 of 10 (immediate-write path covers it). Edit inside a nested ZIP dropped at quit with no message. Project's own test calls flushAll() twice. Server-side variant not run (same upload path).

title: Deleting a member the running flush is writing for the first time is lost
detail: take counts a removal only when record.isInArchive. Lost: a member the running flush is writing for the first time; after a further flushAll the file still listed t/new.txt, member gone from memory, nothing pending; reappears on reopening.
basis: CONFIRMED (ran with hook) for this case

title: Deleting an already-archived member during a flush
detail: Deleting a member that was already in the archive during a flush was persisted by the next flush.
basis: REFUTED (ran with hook) for this case

title: Pack into a server-side or nested ZIP ignores Encrypt
detail: Packing with password = 'pw' into mem:/store/s.zip gave members readable with unzip -p without a password; local control was encrypted.

title: Pack into server-side ZIP removes the old member first; cancel leaves the ZIP empty
detail: Cancelling while a replacement source was being read left the server ZIP empty; the catch block removes the path and flushes. Further, from reading: open.write(path) and blocks(of:) at 498-499 sit outside the do; a source that fails to open leaves the old member removed and the writer never closed.

title: No fsync anywhere in Archives
detail: No fsync, F_FULLFSYNC or synchronize in Plugins/Archives. Power-loss consequence not reproduced.

title: Symlinked archive is replaced by a regular file on edit
detail: No path resolved through symlinks. After an in-archive edit through link.zip -> real/real.zip, link.zip was a regular file holding the change and real.zip unchanged. Packing into the link did the same.

title: Deep member path costs quadratic memory
detail: One implicit entry per ancestor, each with its own full-path string; no depth limit. Measured: depth 2000 +6 MB, 4000 +14 MB, 8000 +56 MB. A real 32 KB ZIP with one member 8000 folders deep cost +77 MB on open. Extrapolated not run: a 65,535-byte ZIP name allows ~32,767 levels, ~1 GB per member; TAR long names not bounded by the format.

title: User regex has no time limit in Selection mask
detail: Plugin states it runs on the main thread. Mask <(a+)+$ on a name of 19/21/23/25 characters took 0.02/0.08/0.32/1.31 s (~4x per two characters). Actual frozen window not reproduced.
basis: CONFIRMED (ran) as mechanism; each run stopped at 25 characters, ~1.3 s

title: User regex has no time limit in Multi-Rename
detail: Same curve (1.27 s at 25 characters). Jobs run one after another; cancel flag only checked between items. Blocked job queue not reproduced.

title: User regex has no time limit in FindFiles content search
detail: Flag checked once per 1 MB block. Cancelled at 0.20 s, the call returned at 1.20 s. Threads spinning long after cancel not reproduced.

title: Long Find text overflows the stack
detail: Recurses once per matched character; search workers are plain Threads with default 512 KB stack. TextPattern.swift compiled alone -O: 5,000 characters found, 6,000 and above crash with bus error; debug build crashes already at 2,000 (lower threshold than reported). Conditions: case-insensitive (default) or whole-words, and a file containing the text or a long prefix. Case-sensitive goes through memmem, fine at 20,000.

title: Multi-Rename nested folders: branch view item names with slash produce doubled subfolder
detail: RenameRun strips the path from an item name only for file: URLs and treats a slash in the new name as a subfolder; branch view names items by path on every file system. Run: item mem:///root/sub/a.txt named sub/a.txt, replacing a->b gave status ready and target mem:///root/sub/sub/b.txt; local control gave a.txt. Rename itself not run.

title: Multi-Rename Undo history limit is not a defect
detail: History is a deliberate 20-run stack, each Undo asks first with list of pairs, spec says MultiRenameUndoHistoryLen 'sets how many operations can be undone'; button disabled while a run is in progress.

title: Numeric trap in SearchCriteria age cutoff
detail: -7 * count; Age(Int.max, .weeks).cutoff trapped. Reaching it needs ~19 digits in 'older than N weeks'.

title: Numeric trap in SearchForm size to String(Int64(size))
detail: String(Int64(size)) for a whole-number Double at or above 2^63 or infinity; reached when a saved search with size 1e19 or inf is loaded. SizeRule.bytes itself is clamped. Not run.

title: Myers cost limit inflates diffs for block moves
detail: Limit is max(256, sqrt(size)) from 20,000 elements; splits at furthest forward point; TextDiff passes no limit. 30,000 lines: 400-line block moved with 2,000 distinct lines: default 58,216 lines in 892 blocks 0.38 s vs shortest 800 in 2 blocks 0.02 s; 3,000-line block moved with 40 distinct lines: 27,104 vs 6,000; 600 inserted and 600 deleted elsewhere: 5,964 vs 1,200. Not inflated: random scattered edits up to 60,000 lines, rewritten section, insertion at front (ratio 1.00-1.01). All results still correct diffs.
basis: CONFIRMED (ran) for block moves; scattered edits not affected

title: Checksum verify skips comment-looking names and reports success on empty/unparsable files
detail: Verify skips lines starting with ; or # while Create writes SFV lines as 'name CRC' unescaped. Create produced ';notes.txt D0AB110E' and '#1 hit.txt DC186425'; after damaging both files Verify reported 'CRC32: Errors: 0', OK: 1. An empty .sfv, binary garbage .md5, prose .sha256 and invalid UTF-16 all report 'Errors: 0', OK: 0.

title: Checksum file with mode 000 reported as OK
detail: A checksum file with mode 000 throws a permission error (the 'unreadable' reading of the claim does not hold).

title: Decode silently truncates: URL-safe Base64 with '--' line
detail: A line starting '--' ends the file though '-' is a valid digit. Decoded 57 of 171 bytes, no error; standard alphabet gave 171.

title: Decode concatenates unpadded numbered neighbours
detail: Decoding IMG_0001.b64 alone wrote 'first file!!SECOND, unrelated!', pulling in IMG_0002.b64; startsFreshFile only recognises headers. Padded control stopped correctly.

title: Decode accepts UUE with a dropped line
detail: 405 of 450 bytes, no error.

title: Decode accepts UUE with missing end
detail: 315 of 450 bytes accepted; finish() closes whatever is open.

title: Decode accepts yEnc with wrong size and crc
detail: A body with =yend size=999999 crc32=deadbeef was accepted.

title: DirectorySync: unreadable left side claimed to give false rows
detail: A mode-000 or missing left side gives no rows and one read error; an unreadable subfolder is left out.

title: DirectorySync: empty left side proposes deleting all right-side files
detail: In asymmetric mode all four right-side files came out rightOnly -> deleteRight and the delete checkbox is pre-ticked. This is what mirror mode means; no guard for an empty or unmounted source.

title: DirectorySync single-item sync errors never shown
detail: Each failure asks Skip / Skip All / Retry / Cancel.

title: DirectorySync commit failures never shown
detail: SyncPlan records them in outcome.errors; SyncSession.finished reads only changedDirectories. Errors after 'Skip All' get no summary either.

title: Cancel after Overwrite deletes pre-existing files in Encode/Split
detail: The list of written files holds the final name, still the old file while the new one is in a temporary; cleanup deletes every name in the list. With existing data.b64 and data.001, answering Overwrite and cancelling during the read left the folder empty for both Encode and Split. A cancel before the writer opens leaves the old file alone.

title: Read-ahead loop re-lists folders the cache refuses
detail: Dwell restarts after every reading; skip only when cache has the folder; cache refuses folders over maxEntries (300,000). With limit set to 30, a 20-entry remote folder listed once in 4 s; a 50-entry one listed 9 times and never remembered. A remote folder over 300,000 entries is listed in full again and again while the cursor rests on it.

title: Reload posts .locationChanged (Quick View dismissed on app activation)
detail: A quiet reload of an unchanged folder and reloadChangedPanels each posted locationChanged. Quick View dismisses on that event for the covered panel; MainWindowController reloads all panels whenever the app becomes active, so switching away and back closes it (from reading).
basis: CONFIRMED (ran events); Quick View dismissal from reading

title: Inline rename cancelled by redraw
detail: redraw() cancels unconditionally. Quiet reloads are held back and the rename survived one. It was cancelled by kernel.panels.refresh (non-quiet reload) and by a sort change; a selection change did not cancel it.

title: Mutually calling user commands loop forever when a wait is in between
detail: em_c = 'em_sayC,cm_wait 20,em_d' and mirror ran 42 lines after 1 s and 83 after 2 s. Guard's active list is popped whenever perform returns for a cm_wait or waited program. Endless loop, not stack recursion. Not run: same through a waited external program with real launches.

title: Mutually calling user commands (direct case)
detail: em_a = 'em_sayA,em_b', em_b = 'em_sayB,em_a' stops with 'a calls itself'.

title: Save As reports success on a short read
detail: Breaks on an empty block and returns nil, so any read that ends early produces a truncated copy with no error. Seen in the claim 3 run.

title: Every local symlink has size 0 so the viewer reads the whole target once just to measure it
detail: lstat-based item(at:) reports size 0 for non-regular files; viewer reads the whole target before showing anything.

title: Packer leaks an open archive writer when the source cannot be opened
detail: From reading only.

title: Verifier run side effects
detail: Trapping tests left swiftpm-testing-helper-2026-10-13-22*.ips crash reports in ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports and may have left a few afm-tests-* folders in the temp directory. Only source change in the scratch copy was one hook between build and install in OpenArchive.flush (claim 6). GUI app never launched.

title: Write outside the target folder: names split on Character so '/' + combining mark hides the separator (archives, decode, combine)
detail: Names are split on Character. A '/' followed by a combining mark is one Character, so the separator is not seen and a leading '..' survives; result is one file written into the parent of the target. Found by a hand-made name after a related mismatch pointed at it, not by mutation runs. Unpacking is a user action so 'high' by the rule; ranked critical as the outside-write case. Reproducers: repro/arch/containment-slash-combining-mark.zip (fuzz-arch, target zip); .tar (target tar); repro/tools/decode-containment-slash-combining-mark.bin (fuzz-tools, decode); repro/tools/combine-containment-slash-combining-mark.crc (fuzz-tools, combine). Same class without a write: RemotePath.normalized in Sources/Plugins/Network/ServerAddress.swift:65 (repro/net/remotepath-slash-joins-combining-mark.bin, fuzz-net, target address).
fix: Split and compare on UTF-8 bytes as RemoteEntry.isSafeName already does, and verify the final URL lies below the target.

title: RemotePath.normalized joins path components across '/' + combining mark (same class, no write)
detail: Same Character-split class as finding 1 but no write; reproducer repro/net/remotepath-slash-joins-combining-mark.bin (fuzz-net, target address).
fix: Split and compare on UTF-8 bytes.

title: Process abort when sorting a listing (CoreFoundation localized compare)
detail: localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare: CoreFoundation's locale compare frees a stack buffer for certain name pairs (128 x U+0015 + U+FFFD + 'a' + 66 x '0' against U+FFFD) on this macOS build. Reproducer repro/misc/sorter-cfcompare-abort.bin (fuzz-misc, target selection); standalone demo in repro/misc/cf/.
fix: Do not hand raw names to the localized compare; strip control characters or compare precomputed sort keys.

title: Hang listing an FTP folder (LIST regex backtracking)
detail: Regexes used by unix(): a LIST line with a long digit run backtracks. 250 / 500 / 1000 / 2000 digits take 15 / 56 / 217 / 991 ms, so a 16 KB line takes about a minute. Reproducer repro/net/ftplist-regex-backtracking.txt (fuzz-net, target ftplist, --timeout 0.5).
fix: Cap the line length and bound the digit runs (\d{1,20}).

title: Shell-quoting command injection through combining-mark characters
detail: ShellWords.escaped compares whole Characters so a ", \, $ or backtick carrying a combining mark is not escaped; a file name of that shape ran an injected command in zsh. Contexts: bare parameters, inside double quotes, %|VAR| and %VAR%; single quotes held. Reproducer repro/misc/quote-injection-combining-mark.bin (fuzz-misc, target quote-demo). 150,800 expansion checks ran through real /bin/zsh -c and /bin/sh -c.
fix: Escape per scalar or byte, or always emit single-quoted words.

title: Unicode trailing spaces trimmed from an expanded name
detail: A name ending in U+00A0 or U+3000 arrives without it so it may name a different file. Reproducers repro/misc/quote-trailing-nbsp-trimmed.bin and quote-trailing-ideographic-space-trimmed.bin.

title: Crash on a saved connection with a negative port
detail: components.port = port; URLComponents traps. Reached through an imported or damaged settings file. Reproducer repro/net/saved-connection-port-trap.json (fuzz-net, target saved).
fix: Validate 1...65535 on decode.

title: Crash in parameter expansion: from + length overflows
detail: from + length overflows for %N:~6,9223372036854775807. Reproducer repro/misc/pexpand-substring-length-overflow.bin (target pexpand).

title: Crash after settings import: frequent-count += 1 on Int.max
detail: += 1 on a stored count of Int.max traps every time that folder is visited. Reproducer repro/misc/settings-import-frequent-count-overflow.json (target settings).

title: Abort saving a selection as ANSI (uncaught NSException)
detail: Foundation raises an uncaught exception for a name such as U+3000 U+0300. Reproducer repro/misc/selection-save-ansi-nsexception.bin (target selection).

title: Two crashes in name templates (New folder / New file) on typed ranges near Int.max/Int.min
detail: last - start + 1 (352) and start + length - 1 (343) overflow. Reproducers repro/diff/nametemplate-slice-overflow.bin and nametemplate-slice-length-overflow.bin (fuzz-diff, target nametemplate).
fix: Limit the digits read, as RenameMask does.

title: Hang in Multi-Rename wildcard/regex backtracking
detail: A plain wildcard search with many * against a 250-letter name becomes a backtracking regex and ran over 60 s; user regex (a*)*b does the same. Preview cannot cancel it. Reproducers repro/diff/renamemask-wildcard-backtracking.bin (target renamemask, --timeout 60) and renameregex-catastrophic.bin (target renameregex).

title: Backwards viewer search returns the match at the start position
detail: Range assumes a match is as long as the needle ('ss' matches 'ß'), so Find Previous would repeat the same hit. Reproducer: FZ_STRICT=1 ... fuzz-viewer run search repro/viewer/search-backwards-returns-match-at-start.bin.

title: Viewer row-index overflow in step *= 2
detail: Overflows when a segment holds more checkpoints than bytes. Critical by the rule (viewing a file) but with the app's 4 MiB segment needs a single line over 268 million rows. Reproducer repro/viewer/rows-thin-overflow.bin (target rows). Patched in the fuzzing copy only (results/PATCHES.txt).

title: Viewer search result depends on path and chunk size with ignorable characters
detail: Two reproducers in repro/viewer/.

title: descript.ion comments misread or lost after an edit
detail: Byte-order-mark collision (55-57) and Character-based parsing (71-76); six reproducers in repro/misc/.

title: PanelModel selection: Set<String> merges NFC/NFD twin names
detail: Reproducer in repro/kernel/ (fuzz-kernel, target panel).

title: PanelModel: a mark without a shown row after setSort
detail: Root cause not analysed. Reproducer in repro/kernel/ (fuzz-kernel, target panel).

title: PanelModel: shown versus listed computed size differs after setComputedSizes
detail: Root cause not analysed. Reproducer in repro/kernel/ (fuzz-kernel, target panel).

title: Byte-identical duplicate names in one listing make totals and selection counts disagree
detail: No minimised reproducer kept.

title: Checksum line '<digest> *' yields an entry with an empty name
detail: Reproducer repro/tools/checksum-empty-name.md5.

title: NameTemplate: empty names from the list branch, and a DateFormatter built per name
detail: About 13 s for <0-99999>[d].

title: Process arguments arrive in decomposed form and './' is prefixed inside the user's quotes
detail: Noted as a low-severity mismatch.

title: FileMask slowest pattern/name pair took 180 ms under ASan
detail: No hang.

title: Archive parsers did not crash, hang or over-allocate in about 2.4 million executions
detail: Group 1 (ziplist, tarlist, tgzlist, txzlist, zip, tar, tgz, txz, zipmod, bz): 1,214,545 asan and 1,142,276 rel executions; no crash, hang or over-memory. HTML viewer rendering is linear. FileMask had no hang. Quoting: single quotes held.

title: bzip2 barely fuzzed
detail: 1,103 executions only, because each input starts /usr/bin/bzip2.

title: Foreign formats (7z, rar, ...) skipped
detail: They go through bsdtar.

title: Sorter thinly fuzzed
detail: About 2,400 executions in the driver; the 8,000-item parallel path and the reference sort make each input slow.

title: FTP session not fuzzed end to end
detail: Only the pure parsers ran; an in-process fake server would be needed.

title: SFTP session depth unconfirmed
detail: The high rate for a process-per-input target (172,155 executions) suggests many inputs ended at connect; depth not confirmed.

title: Absolute-path and symlink-to-absolute escapes not fuzzed
detail: Only relative ways out were seeded.

title: Group 5: imported command steps that open windows were parsed but not performed
Group 6: ProviderByteSource, disk block cache, user-typed regexes and RTF/PDF/image paths not run
Group 7: CompareSession and file-system parts of RenameRun not run
libFuzzer unavailable; custom coverage-guided mutation fuzzer used
detail: -sanitize=fuzzer is unsupported with the Command Line Tools; asan and rel builds, 2 s per input and 2 GB RSS watchdog. One same-line patch in the fuzzing copy (TextRows.swift:225) recorded in results/PATCHES.txt.

title: Left behind: fuzz drivers, scripts, seeds, reproducers, logs under scratchpad review2/fuzz
detail: Build products deleted; rebuild with $F/build.sh rel fuzz-<bin>; drivers in pkg/Fuzz, reproducers in repro/{arch,net,tools,kernel,misc,viewer,diff}, logs summary.log, misc.log, viewer.log, diff.log, PATCHES.txt.

title: listVersion bumped by no-op refresh
detail: setListed -> listChanged() runs before areSameEntries; update(with:) on an identical listing returns false and version still goes 1->2. Other bumps that change no list: setComputedSizes (705), applyFilter with prefiltered list (549). Fallback on main: setSort 5-16 ms at 100k, 60-105 ms CPU (134-175 ms wall) at 1M; setFilter 32 ms at 100k, 355 ms at 1M. With names hitting the slow sort path (claim 15) the sort fallback is single-threaded: 0.67-0.78 s for 200k names.
fix: Bump listVersion only when listedItems actually changed (in update after comparison, not in setComputedSizes, not in applyFilter); when stale, re-dispatch the sort or filter to the background.

title: selectAll / invertSelection / SelectionPlugin on main are O(n)
detail: Linear, at 100k / 1M: selectAll 14 ms / 207 ms; invertSelection 23 ms / 340-442 ms; select(mask:) 18 ms / 216 ms; select all files only (filter+map+setSelected) 55 ms / 919 ms; save+restore selection 22 ms / 358 ms; status-line totals afterwards 12 ms / 212 ms.
fix: Keep marks as a bitset by row index (or 'all except' form) so all/invert/none are O(n/64); keep running selected totals instead of recounting.

title: update(with:) / setListed with filter or marks is expensive on main
detail: At 1M, identical listing, main CPU: no filter no marks 26 ms; filter active 371 ms; all marked 413 ms; filter + 123k marked 808 ms (1.09 s wall). About 10x lower at 100k. Releasing the old array 110 ms at 1M, 10 ms at 100k (not ~0.5 s), on main when oldItems goes out of scope. Release figure lower than claimed.
basis: CONFIRMED (ran); release figure lower than claimed
fix: Do the filter and mark-pruning in the background task that already sorts; hand old arrays to a background queue to free.

title: setComputedSizes with a filter is quadratic
detail: Walks listedItems linearly for every name when a filter is set. For 10,000 sizes with filter active: 1M entries with 10k folders at head 0.38 s (51 ms without filter); 10k folders 0.26 s (1.5 ms); 100k folders 2.97 s (9 ms); 1M folders (1,000 sizes measured) 7.96 s so ~80 s for 10,000 (100 ms without).
fix: Look names up through one dictionary over listedItems, built once per call.

title: Snapshot omits filter and sort
detail: Controller takes the snapshot, dropQuickFilter resets the filter, then open; restore at 657 and 783. Reproduced on the model: after restore 93 items shown of 1000 listed with filter == nil; sort says size-descending while items are in name order. Not a performance issue; persists until next refresh.
fix: Store filter and sort in Snapshot and restore them; controller must restore its quickFilters entry too.

title: Every key validates the whole menu with O(n) closures
detail: On a 240-item menu mainMenu.performKeyEquivalent called validateMenuItem 240 times for an unbound Cmd key, a plain letter and Down-arrow; NSApp.sendEvent of a plain unbound key did the same (no key window; focused-list ordering not proven). Closures: SystemToolsPlugin 54/70 (operands().filter) 26 ms at 100k marked, 390 ms at 1M; ViewOptionsPlugin:128 (!selection.isEmpty builds a Set<String>) 164 ms at 1M on first call after each marks change then cached; ClipboardPlugin:62 hasFiles() 19 ms at 30k files, 57 ms at 100k; NavigationPlugin:132 one pasteboard round trip (not timed). Viewer and MacIntegration closures already cheap.
fix: enabled: { model().directory.isFileURL && model().hasOperandFile } for Print; selectionCount > 0 for Only Selected; cache the pasteboard answer by changeCount; implement menuHasKeyEquivalent(_:for:target:action:) on the menus' delegate.

title: Pasteboard write at drag start and Cmd+C/X is slow on large selections
detail: Linear ~0.1 ms/item on a private pasteboard with real files: writeObjects(NSURL) / drag NSPasteboardItems: 3k 0.43 s / 0.43 s; 10k 1.28 s / 1.45 s; 30k 3.7 s / 3.6 s; 100k 9.8 s / 10.1 s. 300k extrapolates ~30 s, plus operands() 0.3 s at 1M. Process was sandboxed, which may inflate per-URL cost. Worse than claimed.
fix: Write one pasteboard item whose data is provided lazily (NSPasteboardItemDataProvider or single custom-type item holding the list); cap or lazily supply public.file-url entries.

title: Type-to-find is O(n) per key
detail: Table: headless NSTableView asked the delegate for 999,999 rows on one non-matching key: 350 ms at 1M, 34 ms at 100k. Grid TypeSelect.row: 225 ms at 1M, 18 ms at 100k per no-match key. Linear in distance from cursor to match.
fix: Turn off the table's own type select and binary-search the prefix when sorted by name; otherwise search in the background.

title: icon(forFile:) on main per name cell
detail: True but cached by path and date (4,000 entries) and only for visible rows. 40 us per plain file, ~0.2 ms per application. O(visible), not O(n).

title: makeCell() creating cells instead of reusing
detail: Calls makeView(withIdentifier:) first; makeCell is the fallback. What is not reused is the row view (296-299 makes a new CursorRowView every time).

title: reloadData() on every contents change
detail: True. Headless it does not grow with n (0.0 ms at 1M). Whether it causes visible lag is unproven.

title: No minimum interval or back-off on panel re-read
detail: Called at the end of every read.
fix: Re-read no sooner than about max(0.5 s, 2x the last read time) after the previous one.

title: Directory watcher does not coalesce
detail: FSEvents latency 0.5 s did not help: at ~29,000 changes/s, 486-508 callbacks/s reached the main queue, ~50 per 100 ms, each its own queue.async.
fix: Coalesce in Watch.report (one pending flag per watcher).

title: Main thread ~90% busy under a watcher flood
detail: Model work per cycle 26 ms at 1M (up to 0.8 s with filter and marks) against a background read of ~0.75 s CPU for 300k entries. Redraw share needs the running app.

title: Directory tree turns block main longer than budget
detail: 2,000-node budget counts nodes not time. Headless one turn of 2,000 small levels: 10k outline rows 0.27 s; 100k 0.30 s; 1M 0.74-0.81 s. outline.row(forItem:) is O(rows): 0.13 ms per call at 1M. Turns re-queue immediately. Claimed 1.6-1.8 s not reproduced without a window.
basis: CONFIRMED (ran headless) in kind, smaller than claimed
fix: Budget by elapsed time (about 8 ms) and call reloadItem only for expanded nodes, once per turn per node.

title: Multi-Rename reads clipboard and maps rows per keystroke
detail: controlTextDidChange -> refresh() -> makeContext -> clipboard(). Same keystroke runs rows.map(\.entry) on main and apply on main, both O(rows). Not timed.
fix: Read the clipboard once when window activates or changeCount changes.

title: Spotlight results read on main
detail: Reads every result on main. Not timed.
fix: Set metadataQuery.operationQueue and read results there.

title: VirtualFileSystem register/watch are O(n) on main
detail: Linear, at 100k / 1M: register(files:) 83 ms / 0.97 s; watch on a list 127 ms / 1.25 s; registerPicked(operands().map(\.url)) 144 ms / 1.77 s.
fix: Register on the caller's background thread; in watch, stop collecting parents once watchLimit distinct ones are found.

title: FindFiles batching: one folder is one unbounded batch and finish re-passes the model
detail: deliver waits for node.pending == 0 so a folder's hits arrive only when the whole folder is tested; flush only at folder boundaries. On main at 1M (model passes only): append 187 ms; three passes in finish 349 ms. At 100k 10 ms and 15 ms.
fix: Flush by time and size inside onMatch; in finish keep the rows and update only the summary row.

title: Sort comparator is not a strict weak order
detail: Sorter.compareNames rests on localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare, which is asymmetric: 'й' vs 'ий' returns descending in both directions. Russian letters и й е ё И Е я а, names up to 3 letters: 2,268 asymmetric pairs and 48,631 intransitive triples. Also asymmetric for ž in Croatian, ñ in Spanish, å in Danish/Norwegian.
fix: Define the order by the ICU collator itself (sort-key bytes, then name bytes as tie-break); strict weak order by construction, removes the gate, check pass and fallback.

title: Slow sort fallback for non-ASCII names
detail: 200k such names take 0.67-0.78 s on the calling thread against 14 ms for ASCII; result still has thousands of adjacent pairs against the definition. Danish with å/ø 0.57 s. Hungarian ASCII (gate off) 0.43 s vs 0.05 s.

title: ASCII fast-path gate keysOrderPlainNames is unsound
detail: Tests only 2-character names and returned true under da, nb, cy and es@collation=traditional. Pure-ASCII names then sort fast and unchecked, against the definition. Adjacent inversions in 1M names: da/nb 2,868; cy 5,960; es traditional 1,620. Example under Welsh: 'ddd' placed before 'ddf', which the definition orders the other way.

title: Croatian ASCII digraphs (lj, nj) misorder
detail: Not reproduced. Hungarian correctly has the gate off.

title: Static NumberFormatter used across threads
detail: Called off main. Stress test 8 threads x 300,000 calls gave no wrong output and no crash; averaged ~10 us per call. Usage confirmed, harm unproven.
fix: A hand-written digit grouper, also much faster.

title: Modal alerts inside main-queue blocks stall later main-queue work
detail: A nested run loop started inside a DispatchQueue.main.async block does not run later main-queue blocks (timers still fire); started from a timer it does. While such an alert is up every directory piece, sort result and progress update stalls.
fix: Start alerts from a run-loop source (RunLoop.main.perform or CFRunLoopPerformBlock in common modes), or use sheets.

title: Sort or filter with a filter active re-filters on main even on the good path
detail: setSort(_:presorted:) and update go through setListed, which re-filters on main: 378 ms at 1M, 32 ms at 100k.

title: Status line totals recounts all items after any multi-item selection change
detail: 212 ms at 1M.

title: Button and function-key bars revalidate 0.1 s after every window update
detail: With Control held, the function-key bar shows Ctrl+F9 Print and runs the 390 ms operands() closure each time.

title: Quick Look follow calls localOperands() on every panel event
detail: Including each cursor move while the panel is visible: 0.3 s at 1M marked.

title: Paste validation hasFiles() grows with clipboard contents
detail: Copying a large selection makes every later validation slower (see claim 6).

title: Scaling measurement limits
detail: Machine at load average 25-39 on 16 cores so figures are main-thread CPU time unless marked wall. AppKit parts (menu, type-select, outline) ran headless with no window, so they are lower bounds. App never launched; benchmark copy deleted.

title: lockedCopies wipe at 4,096 entries (sub-ruling of claim 10)
detail: Read only, not reproduced. Consequence would be a spurious 'Operation not permitted' on a pending locked temp, not a deletion.

title: lockedCopies: user's own locked original and job-copied locked file are refused (sub-ruling of claim 10)
detail: Not affected: the user's own locked original is refused, and a locked file copied by a job is refused afterwards because the entry is dropped on the temp-to-final rename (461).

title: Local-to-local plain copy of a folder with a named pipe does not hang
detail: It uses copy, not a stream; the pipe was simply not copied.

title: Archive eviction race: stated consequence (data loss then deletion) for file jobs
detail: FileJob.put writes under a temporary name and renames; the rename resolves the archive again, gets a fresh OpenArchive and fails 'not found'; source kept. A commit that succeeds without the data followed by deletion does not follow.

title: Archive eviction race: weaker variant in DirectorySync holds
detail: Sync writes a new file under its final name; commit succeeds as a no-op; data exists only in the orphan until its timer fires; if the app quits first flushAll skips orphans and store.close() deletes the spool. Sync does not delete the source.

title: Autorelease pool claim: 'tens of GB' figure
detail: One pass over a 4 GiB file holds about 4 GiB; tens of GB would need repeated passes without a 2 s pause; not measured in the app.

title: Pool-starvation claim 10: not tested with a real dead mount; quiet reloads do not stack
detail: Only explicit refreshes and navigations add a thread; needs about 80 stuck threads.

title: Password redirect via import (sub-ruling of claim 6)
detail: Password lookup by UUID alone; redirect needs the victim's connection UUID, which is in their own export. Low-medium.

title: Config import: user commands plus key bindings execute code on next keypress; trustedCertificates pre-seeded (sub-ruling of claim 6)
detail: High for the import itself.

title: %|VAR| and %VAR% in Command field are not attacker-controlled in practice (sub-ruling of claim 1)
detail: Affected by the grapheme bug but the value source is the user's own.

title: Names via list file (%L %F %D %UL %UF %WL %WF), cd and cm_ steps, and %Q are not affected (sub-ruling of claim 1)
detail: Names go into a list file or no shell is used; %Q switches quoting off by design.

title: Segment.thin 'never terminates' part
detail: step *= 2 overflows after 62 doublings, so it traps rather than looping forever.

title: Server-side variant of flushAll nested-loss not run
detail: Same upload path as the nested case.

title: FileTools decode/verify/checksum fuzzing: no crash in 556,778 asan and 416,655 rel executions
detail: Containment fails in decode and combine (finding 1); one low mismatch (checksum empty name).

title: Kernel group: no trap in 917,259 asan and 1,053,579 rel executions
detail: Only 3 low PanelModel mismatches; a Sorter abort was found via group 5.

title: Viewer group: HTML rendering is linear
detail: 722,561 asan and 3,592,721 rel executions; 1 trap, 2 search bugs.

title: Network group executions
detail: 3,515,177 asan and 3,047,481 rel executions: 1 crash, 1 hang, 1 mismatch.

title: Misc group executions
detail: 883,773 asan and 726,860 rel: 4 crashes, quoting injection. Diff/rename group 488,763 asan and 639,799 rel: 2 crashes, 2 hangs.

title: Viewer and MacIntegration menu closures already use cheap tests
detail: Not a cost source for per-key validation.

title: Menu validation for a list with focus
detail: Headless run had no key window; same ordering for a focused list not proven.
